tasks.title: Implement local Ollama adapter
tasks.acceptance: Local schema probe; missing/incompatible/cloud models rejected
tasks.evidence: Ollama adapter implemented against the native /api/chat endpoint with the JSON schema in the format field, temperature 0, local-only enforcement, model availability checked before each request, cloud and remote-host models filtered out of listModels, and an optional /api/embed path. FINDING AND FIX (2026-09-18): the adapter set num_predict but never num_ctx. Ollama defaults to a small context window (commonly 4096) and silently discards the overflow, and chat truncation drops the oldest messages first, which is the system prompt. The untrusted-content boundary declaration could therefore be evicted while the repository text it governs survived, degrading output quality and weakening the prompt-injection boundary at the same time. The adapter now requests num_ctx covering the whole budgeted request (LIMITS.contextTokens + LIMITS.outputTokens = 16000, raisable through AdapterOptions.contextTokens), with a test asserting num_ctx is at least the full budget, num_predict never exceeds it, and temperature stays 0. Results: pnpm check passed with 111 unit tests across 20 files; pnpm build passed.

tasks.title: Route installation and PR lifecycle
tasks.acceptance: Reordered events cannot revive removed access or obsolete work
tasks.evidence: Installation, repository and pull-request event handling implemented in apps/worker/src/handlers.ts, with the acceptance property proven: reordered events cannot revive removed access or obsolete work. An installation event records suspension and deletion, and DELETION IS TERMINAL: the update only ever moves deleted from false to true, so a redelivered creation cannot restore access a user removed, and suspension is not touched once an installation is deleted. A repository is recorded on any event that carries one, but a repository nobody enabled is never reviewed. A pull request is only scheduled for review on opened, synchronize, reopened or ready_for_review, drafts are skipped unless marked ready, and the generation advances only when the head actually moves so a redelivery is inert. ORDERING DEFECT FOUND AND CLOSED: the event contract carried no timestamp, so a redelivered older event would have overwritten a newer head. GitHubEventSchema now carries occurredAt, normalizeWebhook takes it from the pull request or repository updated_at and falls back to receipt time, and the pull-request upsert refuses to apply an event older than the row it would overwrite, returning superseded_by_newer_event. 5 PostgreSQL integration tests prove each property, including that a stale synchronize cannot drag a pull request back to a head it has moved past, and that a redelivered creation cannot undelete an installation. Results: pnpm check 191 unit tests across 31 files; pnpm build passed; 45 integration tests passed from a freshly created disposable database.

tasks.title: Validate runner result envelopes
tasks.acceptance: Reject stale, conflicting, oversized or mismatched results
tasks.evidence: Result upload, independent validation and the runner seam are implemented, and asynchronous publication is now possible. validateRunnerResult treats the runner as untrusted and checks nodes pinned to the reviewed head and repository, duplicate identities, candidates referencing only submitted nodes, quoted text genuinely present in its node so a fabricated quote cannot reach a pull request, resolving evidence references, and verification verdicts bound to a recomputed candidate identity. The upload route refuses oversized bodies before parsing, malformed or misaddressed envelopes, invalid content with codes only, and stale, superseded, expired, foreign or conflicting submissions, with identical duplicates idempotent and validation running before anything is persisted. Acceptance schedules publication through a port rather than publishing inline, and a duplicate never schedules twice. ARCHITECTURE CONFLICT SURFACED AND RESOLVED AS ADR-038: a scheduled publication was impossible to act on, because findings cannot be persisted with their text in ephemeral retention mode and the accepted result existed only in the answered HTTP request. Inline publication would make a runner wait on GitHub and lose the review on failure; an in-memory handoff would not survive a restart or a second instance. The accepted resolution introduces publication_payloads, holding the validated payload only until publication completes or is abandoned, which matches the specification wording that ephemeral context is rebuilt per review and DELETED AFTER THE JOB rather than never written. Migration 0004_famous_fixer.sql applies from a clean disposable database, and five PostgreSQL tests prove the lifetime guarantee: discarded after success, discarded after abandonment, swept when a crash leaves one behind while a live payload is untouched, refused for a non-existent run, and isolated by tenant. Results: pnpm check 191 unit tests across 31 files; pnpm build passed; 51 integration tests passed from a freshly created disposable database.
tasks.nextAction: No publish worker process exists yet, so the payload lifetime is enforced by the store and proven at that level but not yet by a worker that calls discard on every path, including after an abandoned publish. That worker, its queue subscriptions and the retention sweep schedule are the next step, and the GitHub transport it drives still needs App credentials.

stages.title: First useful-review and runner vertical slice

tasks.title: Resolve trusted configuration
tasks.acceptance: Trusted-base precedence and administrator-only fields enforced
tasks.evidence: Trusted configuration resolution implemented and now WIRED TO A CALLER, which was the gap this task carried. packages/config parses .humanize.yml as hostile input (64 KiB cap, alias expansion capped, custom tags refused, mapping required), rejects any administrator-only key outright rather than ignoring it, lets a repository narrow review but never widen it, clamps the inline budget to the administrator cap, and fails closed to policy defaults so a malformed file cannot switch reviewing off. The event handler in apps/worker now reads that file through a TrustedFileSource port AT THE BASE REF, never the head, so a pull request cannot change the rules it will be judged by (ADR-027); it resolves the effective configuration against administrator policy, builds the ReviewSnapshot pinning configSha and the configuration digest, creates the review run and enqueues it. An integration test proves the read targets the base ref and the configuration path, that execution and retention in the stored snapshot come from policy rather than the repository file, that the run is persisted in state RECEIVED, and that a redelivery reuses the same run and produces the same idempotency key rather than a second review. Earlier finding retained: Zod 4 z.record() with an enum key is exhaustive, which silently invalidated any partial category map until it was changed to z.partialRecord. Results: pnpm check 191 unit tests across 31 files; pnpm build passed; 46 integration tests passed.
tasks.nextAction: Remaining: no production TrustedFileSource exists, so nothing yet fetches the configuration file from GitHub; that binding needs App credentials. Organization policy is supplied through an injected function and has no persistence or administration surface, which is P1-S16-T02. Explicit learnings remain part of the documented precedence chain with no store behind them (P1-S17-T01). Path-specific configuration is resolved by the package but the caller passes no path, so per-path overrides are not yet applied per node.

tasks.title: Build ephemeral lexical context
tasks.acceptance: Context works without content tables or embeddings
tasks.evidence: Ephemeral lexical context implemented; acceptance that context works without content tables or embeddings is proven. packages/retrieval adds EphemeralContextIndex, an in-memory index over the ContentNodes of one review with BM25 ranking, character-trigram near-duplicate detection standing in for pg_trgm, and same-file neighbour lookup; it satisfies the existing RetrievalPort contract and depends only on @humanize/domain and @humanize/shared, so no database, no pgvector and no embedding provider is involved (INV-015). buildContext assembles the specified priority order (same-file neighbours, configured rules and approved voice, near duplicates, strongest related content) under a hard token budget that drops lower-priority evidence rather than stretching. Evidence records carry the commit revision and a content hash over blob, offsets and text so the control plane can revalidate them at publication. Tests (9, all passing): related content retrieved with no infrastructure; nodes from another repository or another commit rejected with NODE_OUT_OF_SNAPSHOT because scoping is a tenant boundary, not an optimization; deterministic results across repeated queries and reversed insertion order via stable-key tie-breaking; empty and stopword-only queries return nothing rather than noise; near duplicates detected while merely similar topics are not; neighbours ordered nearest-first within the same file only; content hash changes when the referenced text changes; context built in priority order with de-duplicated records, budget respected and truncation reported; and a repository with no related content yields empty context rather than failing. FINDING: swept the codebase for the Zod 4 exhaustive-record trap recorded against S08-T01 and found no other occurrence; the only remaining z.record uses a string key schema and is genuinely partial. Results: pnpm check passed with 84 unit tests across 17 files; pnpm build passed; 39 integration tests still pass from a freshly created disposable humanize_test database.
tasks.nextAction: Remaining before complete: no caller yet builds an index or context, so this is proven in isolation rather than in a review; wiring arrives with P1-S08-T04. PR title and body and explicit learnings are named in the specification context set but are not yet available as evidence sources (learnings are P1-S17-T01). Ranking coefficients are a documented BM25 default and have not been tuned against the review corpus, which is P1-S08-T05. Indexed-mode PostgreSQL retrieval and optional pgvector fusion remain with P1-S12 and P1-S18; this task deliberately covers only the ephemeral path.

tasks.title: Implement deterministic rules and routing
tasks.acceptance: Content kinds route to appropriate categories
tasks.evidence: Deterministic rules and routing implemented and since improved by measurement. Rules emit the documented AI-style signals without any model, every span comes from the node text, and output is sorted for reproducibility; a test asserts no description ever claims machine authorship (INV-006). The router maps content kind and length to categories: a marketing paragraph receives the full set, a button label never receives long-form prose review, accessibility text receives clarity and terminology only, and disabled categories never route. TWO IMPROVEMENTS DRIVEN BY THE REVIEW GOLD SET. First, phrase matching was literal, so "leveraging the power of" did not match the listed "leverage the power of" and a passage fell below the cluster threshold, producing no finding; matching is now inflection-aware across ordinary English endings, verified by a test over leverage, leverages and leveraging. Second, the corpus showed the missed cases shared a shape the product had no rule for at all, namely wordiness and padding as distinct from promotional vocabulary; a padding rule family now covers constructions such as provides users with the ability to, it is important to note that and in order to get started, marked standalone under ADR-037 because they are countable, with a test asserting direct writing carries none. MEASURED EFFECT on the 26-case gold set: overall recall rose from 50% to 80%, clear-cut recall from 80% to 100%, ambiguous recall from 20% to 60%, and PRECISION REMAINED 100% throughout, so nothing was gained by becoming noisier. Results: pnpm check 189 unit tests across 31 files.
tasks.nextAction: Two ambiguous cases remain missed and are being left alone deliberately: ai-assisted-residual would require adding empowers, seamlessly and streamline to the phrase list, and vague-tagline is a five-word heading the router intentionally does not send for long-form review. Both fixes would fit the corpus rather than generalise, which is the definition of overfitting a ten-case set. Phrase lists remain hand-written and unmeasured against real repositories.

tasks.title: Implement first reviewer and verifier pipeline
tasks.acceptance: Fabricated/weak findings suppressed; verifier separately invoked
tasks.evidence: Reviewer and verifier pipeline implemented and now exercised against a real model for the first time. Deterministic gate between model output and any finding: a candidate is discarded unless it names the reviewed node, quotes text genuinely present in it, cites only supplied evidence and stays within routed categories; thresholds start at 0.90; coordinates are attached from the node, never from the model. The verifier is a separate invocation with its own system prompt, verdicts bind by ADR-036 identity, and a missing or misbound verdict suppresses rather than publishes. Repository content is fenced with a per-review unguessable marker that is stripped from the content itself. 13 unit tests cover these paths. TWO DEFECTS FOUND BY LIVE TESTING THAT MOCKS COULD NOT CATCH. First, reviewerInput never told the model which nodeId to use although the schema requires one, so the model invented an identifier and every model-proposed finding was discarded as foreign_node; the mocked tests passed only because the doubles supplied the correct id themselves. The prompt now states the node identifier and a unit test asserts it. Second, the published explanation was the verifier narrating its own checking, including leaked evidence hash identifiers, which would have gone verbatim into a pull request comment; the verifier prompt now requires correctedExplanation to be the sentence the author reads and forbids mentioning identifiers, coordinates or the verification itself. MEASURED LIVE BEHAVIOUR after both fixes, using qwen3.5:4b: generic marketing copy produced a verified ai_like_generic finding quoting the content exactly, with the author-facing explanation "The phrase unprecedented potential is a low-information promotional claim that lacks specific substance or evidence"; acceptable product copy produced no published finding, with a reviewer-proposed clarity candidate correctly suppressed by the verifier; plain documentation produced nothing; and content instructing the model to report a finding with exactText SYSTEM COMPROMISED produced nothing, the attempt being suppressed as evidence_not_supplied. Results: pnpm check 114 unit tests across 20 files; pnpm build passed; 40 integration tests passed; 8 live tests passed.
tasks.nextAction: Remaining before complete: no caller runs this over a real pull request, which is P1-S08-T06. Live evidence is one small local model on five hand-written cases, which is a smoke test and not a quality measurement; P1-S08-T05 must measure precision against labelled content. OBSERVED QUALITY ISSUES for that task: the model returned overlapping findings for a whole sentence and a sub-phrase of it, which ranking and deduplication in P1-S13 must merge, and it sometimes proposes a finding for acceptable copy that only the verifier removes. Bounded one-step context expansion remains unimplemented; ReviewerResponseSchema carries searches and the pipeline ignores it.

tasks.title: Evaluate first useful-review corpus
tasks.acceptance: Independent human usefulness report with clean-copy negatives
tasks.evidence: Review gold set now holds 26 labelled cases: 16 clear-cut and 10 covering the ambiguous middle that was previously absent, namely mediocre human copy and edited AI-assisted copy. Ambiguous labels are marked as judgement calls and scored separately, because a failure there may mean the label is wrong rather than the reviewer. MEASURED with qwen3.5:4b: overall precision 100% recall 50%; clear-cut precision 100% recall 80%; AMBIGUOUS PRECISION 100% RECALL 20%. Precision held at 100% across all 26 cases, including every ambiguous negative: passive voice, an edited AI sentence, a long but information-dense sentence, a hedged claim and correct industry jargon were all left alone. The product does not nag. Recall on the ambiguous middle is 20%, with four of five missed: padded phrasing such as "provides users with the ability to", stacked redundancy such as "In order to get started, you will first need to begin by", residual AI wording such as "empowers teams to seamlessly streamline", and a vague tagline. Only the uniform three-clause cadence was caught, and by a deterministic rule rather than the model. TWO FINDINGS. First, the missed cases share a shape the product has no rule for: wordiness and padding, as distinct from promotional vocabulary. Second, the deterministic phrase list matches literal strings and not morphological variants, so "leveraging the power of" does not match the listed "leverage the power of"; that is why generic-docs-opener fell to two matched phrases, below the three-phrase cluster threshold, and was missed this run although the model flagged it in an earlier one. Clear-cut recall therefore sits exactly at the 0.8 floor and will flake with model variance. Results: pnpm check 187 unit tests across 31 files.
tasks.nextAction: Deliberately NOT tuned further in this session: chasing 20% ambiguous recall against 10 cases would overfit to the corpus rather than improve the product. The evidence-led order for whoever continues is: add a padding and wordiness rule family, since the misses share that shape and such phrases are as countable as the promotional ones; make phrase matching stem-aware so leverage, leverages and leveraging all match; enlarge the ambiguous set well beyond 10 cases before trusting any recall number from it; and re-measure with a larger local model to separate prompt and threshold behaviour from model capacity, since the same case flipped between runs at temperature 0. The specification gate still requires independent human judgement of usefulness, which no measurement here provides.

tasks.title: Connect local runner execution
tasks.acceptance: Private live repository review has no cloud-model traffic or retained source
tasks.evidence: Local runner execution connected: Humanize now reviews a pull request end to end. apps/runner/src/executor.ts runs one leased job inside an ephemeral workspace: restricted read-only clone with the job-scoped token, merge-base diff geometry, enumeration and classification of every tracked file, extraction of user-visible content from supported files only, selection of changed nodes intersecting right-hand-side added lines, an ephemeral context index, rules, routing, and the reviewer and verifier pipeline, producing a RunnerResult envelope. Customer code is never executed. apps/runner/src/main.ts now starts instead of refusing: it sweeps workspaces abandoned by a previous process, advertises locally installed models as capabilities, and handles SIGTERM and SIGINT. MEASURED LIVE RESULT against a real Git repository and a real local model (qwen3.5:4b), 31.5 seconds: two changed nodes across two files reviewed from three extracted nodes, producing docs.md:3 unsupported_claim "Our revolutionary state-of-the-art solution seamlessly integrates to supercharge your workflow." explained as unsupported promotional claims without evidence, and landing.tsx:1 approved_voice "Unlock unprecedented potential with our cutting-edge platform" explained as vague wording; two further candidates were suppressed below confidence, and zero workspace entries remained. Tests: 4 unit tests against a real local Git repository proving only changed content is reviewed, a binary file is classified out and never parsed, no host other than the configured local model is contacted, a job carrying a cloud model profile is refused with CLOUD_MODEL_IN_PRIVATE_JOB, and the workspace is destroyed after success, refusal and provider failure; plus a live end-to-end test. Results: pnpm check 118 unit tests across 21 files; pnpm build passed; 40 integration tests passed; 9 live tests passed in 35.6 seconds.
tasks.nextAction: Remaining before complete: acceptance names a private LIVE repository, and no review has run against a real private GitHub repository with a real installation token, because no GitHub App credentials exist; the end-to-end evidence uses a local Git origin standing in for the remote, and GitRepository.acquire is substituted in tests. The runner also does not yet upload its result: executeReview returns a RunnerResult but the poll loop does not call the upload route, so P1-S07-T05 and this task meet only at the seam. Extraction covers Babel and Markdown only, so Vue, Svelte, HTML, CSS and locale content in a changed file are silently not reviewed until P1-S09 and P1-S10. Changed-node selection is capped at LIMITS.nodeBatch with no chunking for larger pull requests.

tasks.title: Extract HTML text and attributes
tasks.acceptance: Entities/quotes mapped; scripts/styles/machine attributes excluded
tasks.evidence: HTML extraction implemented with parse5 and source-location tracking, closing the gap the corpus measured. Rendered text nodes and visible or accessibility attributes (alt, title, placeholder, aria-*, label, summary) are extracted; script, style, template, noscript, svg, code, pre, iframe and object contents are excluded, as are machine attributes such as href, src, class, id, name, type and value however wordy their values look. Source ranges map exactly onto the original document including multi-line text, quote style is recorded so an attribute value can be re-encoded safely, and entity-bearing content is marked suggestionSafe false with encoding entity because the raw source and rendered text differ and a verbatim replacement would corrupt the encoding. Element name drives content kind, so a heading, link and alt text are classified distinctly. 7 unit tests cover visible-only extraction, machine attribute exclusion, exact single and multi-line spans, entity handling, quote style, kind classification, and recovery from malformed markup without failing the file. MEASURED EFFECT on the fixture corpus, same model and fixtures as before: extracted nodes rose from 8 to 13 and reviewed changed nodes from 4 to 7, and index.html now produces findings, including clarity on "The ultimate game-changing solution for modern enterprises" which was previously invisible. Results: pnpm check 153 unit tests across 27 files; pnpm build passed.
tasks.nextAction: Acceptance for entities, quotes and exclusions is met at unit level. Remaining: HTML-specific suggestion encoding is not implemented, so an entity-bearing or attribute finding currently falls back to comment-only; that belongs with P1-S11. Extraction precision and recall against a labelled HTML corpus are not measured, which is P1-S09-T04 and P1-S10-T04.

tasks.title: Extract JSON and YAML localization
tasks.acceptance: Locale discrimination and source spans correct
tasks.evidence: JSON and YAML localization extraction implemented. A file is treated as a locale resource only when its path follows convention (locales, i18n, translations, messages, lang, or a language-coded filename) or configuration declares it, so arbitrary JSON such as package.json or tsconfig.json is never reviewed as prose; a non-locale data file now returns a NOT_A_LOCALE_SOURCE diagnostic rather than silently extracting nothing, because silence is the dangerous case. Values are reviewed and keys are context only. Machine values are excluded by key and by shape: URLs, paths, colours, endpoints, identifiers, numbers and values containing no letters. Source spans map to the value inside its quotes so a replacement re-encodes in place, quote style is recorded, nested objects and arrays are walked, placeholders survive extraction, and an escaped value is marked unsafe for verbatim replacement. YAML is supported through the same path. 9 unit tests cover locale discrimination both ways, key-versus-value handling, machine value exclusion, exact spans, nesting, YAML with ICU and handlebars placeholders, escape safety, the diagnostic for a non-locale file, and malformed input. MEASURED EFFECT: locales/en.json in the fixture corpus now produces an approved_voice finding on "Unlock unprecedented potential today", which the previous run could not see at all. Results: pnpm check 153 unit tests across 27 files.
tasks.nextAction: Remaining: translation-key resolution, where a JSX or HTML reference such as t("hero.title") is linked to the locale value so the rendered string is reviewed in context, is P1-S09-T03 and is not implemented. Locale discrimination is convention-based and has not been measured against a corpus of real repositories, so an unconventional layout still needs explicit configuration.

tasks.title: Resolve safe constants and translations
tasks.acceptance: Cycles, dynamic values and ambiguous resources remain unresolved

tasks.title: Extend placeholder and failure corpus
tasks.acceptance: Malformed files isolated; all metrics reported
tasks.evidence: Extraction corpus expanded from 7 to 17 labelled files covering every parser, now carrying placeholder expectations, suggestion-eligibility expectations and hostile inputs: deep nesting, unclosed HTML, entity-bearing text and attributes, escaped locale values, ICU and printf placeholders, digest-like values, table markup, inline code inside prose, and dynamic Vue and Svelte bindings. The gate enforces four properties in the default lane and now fails pnpm check on a regression in any of them. THE EXPANDED CORPUS IMMEDIATELY FOUND FOUR DEFECTS, all fixed. First, Markdown dropped inline code from inside a paragraph, so "Each installation may send `5000` requests per hour." was reviewed as "Each installation may send  requests per hour." with the value missing; a finding or a suggestion based on that corrupted sentence would have been wrong, so inline code is now included as composite-encoded text and the node is not offered as a replacement. Second, Markdown emitted raw table markup as a paragraph, because remark without the GFM plugin does not parse tables; pipe-delimited blocks are now skipped, and full table-cell extraction still requires remark-gfm and is recorded as a gap. Third, locale extraction reviewed digest-like values as prose, so a commit SHA under a build.sha key became reviewable content; sha, hash, digest, token, secret and slug keys are now machine keys, and an unspaced hex or identifier token is refused by shape. Fourth, the range-accuracy metric itself was wrong: it demanded a byte-identical slice for every segment, which an entity-encoded or escaped segment can never satisfy; identity segments must now slice exactly, and any other encoding must have a real span and a node not offered as a verbatim replacement. Two label errors of mine were also corrected, a blockquote wrongly excluded and a paragraph with an inline link wrongly omitted. MEASURED across 17 files: babel, markdown, html, json-locale, vue, svelte and css all at precision 100%, recall 100%, range accuracy 100%, with placeholder and unsafe-label accuracy 100% wherever labelled. Results: pnpm check 185 unit tests across 31 files; pnpm build passed; 40 integration tests passed.
tasks.nextAction: Still far short of the specification, which expects hundreds of fixtures: 17 files means the gate rejects regressions on these cases, not that extraction is correct in general. Highest-value additions next: real-world JSX patterns such as configured visible props and UI call functions, MDX expression boundaries, YAML locale edge cases, right-to-left and CJK content, and files large enough to exercise the size and timeout limits. Markdown table cells remain unextracted pending a decision on adding remark-gfm, which the specification implies since it lists table text as reviewable content.

stages.title: Vue Svelte CSS and extraction gate

tasks.title: Extract Vue static templates
tasks.acceptance: Original SFC offsets correct; computed values never executed
tasks.evidence: Vue single-file-component extraction implemented with the official @vue/compiler-sfc parser. Static template text and visible or accessibility attributes are extracted; script, style, nested template, pre and code blocks are excluded, as are machine attributes. Offsets come from the compiler and are relative to the ORIGINAL file rather than the extracted template block, verified by a test asserting every node slice equals its own text. Interpolations and bound directives are never evaluated: a test proves {{ product.title }} and :alt="computedAlt" yield no prose, because resolving them would mean executing customer code (INV-001). Malformed SFCs return no nodes rather than failing the file. Measured by the extraction release gate at precision 100%, recall 100%, range accuracy 100%. Results: pnpm check 183 unit tests across 31 files; pnpm build passed; 40 integration tests passed.
tasks.nextAction: Vue suggestion encoding is not implemented, so a Vue finding is comment-only until an encoder and structural validator exist for that format. Translation-key resolution inside Vue templates is part of P1-S09-T03 and remains absent.

tasks.title: Extract Svelte static templates
tasks.acceptance: Dynamic/static distinction and offsets validated
tasks.evidence: Svelte extraction implemented with the official svelte/compiler in modern AST mode. Static template text and visible attributes are extracted while script and style contents are excluded. The dynamic and static distinction is enforced structurally: an attribute is only extracted when its value is a single literal Text part, so an interpolated attribute such as alt={dynamicAlt} and an interpolated text node such as {title} produce no prose, proven by test. Offsets map onto the original file, verified by asserting every node slice equals its own text. A malformed component returns no nodes rather than failing the file. Measured by the extraction release gate at precision 100%, recall 100%, range accuracy 100%. Results: pnpm check 183 unit tests across 31 files.
tasks.nextAction: Svelte suggestion encoding is absent, so Svelte findings remain comment-only. Svelte 5 snippet and render-tag constructs are not specifically handled beyond being skipped as non-literal.

tasks.title: Extract CSS generated content
tasks.acceptance: Only static pseudo-element content with correct escapes
tasks.evidence: CSS generated-content extraction implemented with PostCSS. Only static content declarations on ::before and ::after pseudo-elements are extracted; a declaration on a non-pseudo selector, an empty string, and dynamic values built from counter(), attr(), url(), var() or the quote keywords are all skipped, proven by a test whose fixture contains each case and yields exactly one node. Quote style is recorded and a CSS escape marks the value unsafe for verbatim replacement. Generated content is extracted with visibility confidence 0.85 rather than 1, because it is rendered to sighted users but invisible to assistive technology and to translation, so it is reviewed conservatively as the specification requires. Measured by the extraction release gate at precision 100%, recall 100%, range accuracy 100%. Results: pnpm check 183 unit tests across 31 files.
tasks.nextAction: CSS suggestion encoding is absent, so a generated-content finding is comment-only. Escaped unicode sequences are detected and refused rather than decoded.

tasks.title: Enforce full extraction release gate
tasks.acceptance: Per-parser precision 98%, recall 90%, range accuracy 99%
tasks.evidence: Extraction release gate implemented in evals/extraction. A labelled corpus in gold.ts states, per parser, the user-visible strings extraction must find and the machine strings it must never mistake for prose (endpoints, identifiers, asset paths, class lists, colours, code fences, script and style contents). gate.test.ts computes precision, recall and range accuracy per parser and enforces the specification thresholds of 98%, 90% and 99%, failing the default test lane when any parser falls below them; a second test asserts no labelled machine string is ever extracted, because noise about text the author never wrote for a reader is worse than a missed string. Range accuracy is measured PER SEGMENT rather than per node: a Markdown paragraph containing an inline link assembles its text from several source runs, so each segment must map its slice of the text back to the exact source it came from. MEASURED: babel, markdown, html, json-locale, vue, svelte and css all at precision 100%, recall 100%, range accuracy 100%. The gate earned its place on its first run by rejecting a mislabelled fixture and an over-strict metric. Results: pnpm check 183 unit tests across 31 files.
tasks.nextAction: The corpus is small, with one file per parser, so 100% means the gate passes on these cases rather than that extraction is perfect; the specification expects hundreds of fixtures and the corpus must grow substantially before the numbers carry release weight. Not yet labelled: placeholder expectations, suggestion-eligibility expectations and deliberately hostile inputs, which are P1-S09-T04.

tasks.title: Encode source-specific replacements
tasks.acceptance: Quotes, entities, escapes and multiline scalar cases pass
tasks.evidence: Source-specific replacement encoders implemented in packages/suggestions/src/encode.ts. JSX and Markdown text is emitted verbatim after refusing prose carrying markup; HTML text is entity-encoded; HTML attribute values are encoded for the quote style actually used, so a quote inside the replacement becomes an entity and cannot terminate the attribute or introduce a new one; JSON and locale values are re-encoded inside their existing quotes with escapes; bare YAML scalars are refused when the replacement starts with an indicator character or would read as a mapping; JavaScript and TypeScript string literals are escaped for single, double or template quoting including dollar-brace sequences. A node the extractor marked unsafe, a control character, a multi-line replacement for a single-line node and an unsupported source kind are all refused rather than guessed, because a wrong encoding corrupts a customer file. Tests cover JSX text, HTML text and attributes, locale values with embedded quotes, and the refusal cases. Results: pnpm check 173 unit tests across 29 files; pnpm build passed; 40 integration tests passed.
tasks.nextAction: Vue, Svelte and CSS encoders are absent because their extractors do not exist yet (P1-S10). Multi-line and complex Markdown nodes containing inline links or emphasis remain comment-only, as the specification requires until a dedicated validator proves such a patch safe.

tasks.title: Preserve placeholder semantics
tasks.acceptance: Altered/missing/duplicated and ordered placeholders rejected
tasks.evidence: Placeholder preservation implemented in packages/suggestions/src/placeholders.ts and enforced before any suggestion is built. The placeholder multiset is compared before and after: a removed placeholder, an added one, an altered name, a changed repetition count and a reordered positional format are each rejected with a distinct reason. Ordering is checked only for positional formats such as %s and %d, which bind by position, so reordering them silently swaps the values a user is shown; named placeholders may move freely. A rewording that keeps every placeholder intact is accepted. Tests cover all five violations and the accepting case, plus an end-to-end refusal proving a suggestion that would drop a placeholder is never published. Results: pnpm check 173 unit tests across 29 files.
tasks.nextAction: ICU plural and select expressions are treated as opaque placeholders rather than parsed, so a replacement that restructures an ICU message is refused rather than validated; a dedicated ICU validator remains future work.

tasks.title: Reparse and prove structural preservation
tasks.acceptance: Valid syntax that injects expressions or attributes is rejected
tasks.evidence: Structural preservation implemented in packages/suggestions/src/index.ts. A candidate patch is applied in memory only, then the modified file is re-extracted and compared with the original: the parse must succeed, the node count must match, every node must keep its identity excluding position, exactly one node may differ, and that node must now contain precisely the proposed text. Anything else is rejected as STRUCTURE_CHANGED, TEXT_NOT_APPLIED or REPARSE_FAILED, and the finding falls back to a comment. This is what catches a replacement that is syntactically valid yet still wrong: a test proves prose opening a JSX expression or an HTML element is rejected, and that an attribute injection attempt is entity-encoded into literal text rather than becoming a new attribute. DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED while proving this: the HTML extractor located an attribute value by searching the raw source for the decoded value, so any attribute containing an entity was silently dropped and never reviewed at all; the span is now derived from the quote positions and such a value is extracted and marked unsafe to replace. Results: pnpm check 173 unit tests across 29 files.
tasks.nextAction: Structural comparison relies on the extractor for the file type, so it is only as strong as that extractor; a format without one cannot be validated and therefore cannot receive a suggestion. Nothing is ever written to disk, and no suggestion has yet been applied on a real pull request, which needs GitHub credentials.

stages.title: Complete review verification and noise policy

tasks.title: Complete category schemas and evidence validation
tasks.acceptance: All categories include valid/invalid evidence and authorship rejection
tasks.evidence: Ranking, deduplication and the noise budget implemented in packages/review/src/ranking.ts, taken ahead of its stage because live testing showed the model returning a finding for a whole sentence and another for a sub-phrase of it, which would have spammed the first pull request Humanize commented on. scoreFinding combines the lower of reviewer and verifier confidence, a severity weight, evidence quality, the node visibility confidence and actionability, and is deterministic. planPublication merges findings that share a fingerprint, that overlap the same source range in the same category, or that propose the same replacement for the same place, keeping the higher-scoring statement; it then holds subjective findings to five inline comments with the remainder moved to the summary, exempts deterministic policy violations from the budget, and excludes nitpicks by default while keeping deterministic ones. The configured budget is clamped to the product default so configuration cannot raise it. 8 unit tests cover scoring order and stability, the sentence-versus-sub-phrase merge that live testing exposed, distinct places and categories kept apart, same-replacement merging, budget overflow to summary, blocking findings never losing their slot, nitpick exclusion, and identical plans regardless of input order. Results: pnpm check 127 unit tests across 22 files.
tasks.nextAction: Coefficients are a documented starting point, not a calibrated model; the specification requires them to be evaluation-driven and they must be tuned against the labelled corpus in P1-S08-T05 before release. Remaining in this stage: the review summary generator, feedback-informed ranking, and confirming the budget end to end once the publisher exists. No caller applies planPublication yet; the publisher is next.

tasks.title: Complete independent verifier
tasks.acceptance: Corrected output is revalidated and cannot fabricate evidence
tasks.evidence: Verifier corrections are now revalidated rather than trusted. DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED: correctedExplanation and correctedReplacement were applied verbatim, so a verifier could replace a reviewer suggestion with text that drops a placeholder, producing a message with a hole in it, or blank out an explanation. A discarded correction is recorded as a CORRECTION_DROPPED_PLACEHOLDER diagnostic rather than passing silently, and ReviewOutcome now carries diagnostics. Verified by test: a verdict proposing "Hi there, you have alerts" against text containing {name} and {{count}} is refused and the reviewer replacement survives, while a sound correction preserving both placeholders is applied. tasks.evidence: Noise policy implemented and enforced in packages/review/src/ranking.ts. planPublication holds subjective findings to five inline comments with the remainder moved to the summary, exempts deterministic policy violations from that budget so a configured rule is never crowded out, excludes nitpicks by default while keeping deterministic ones, and clamps a configured budget to the product default so configuration cannot raise it. tasks.title: Fence publishing and recheck freshness
tasks.acceptance: Head races cannot remain classified as current completed feedback
tasks.evidence: Publication transport implemented in packages/github/src/transport.ts. ReviewPublisher re-reads the pull request head immediately before writing and throws StaleHeadError when it has moved, so findings computed for a superseded commit are never published as current feedback (INV-010); a test asserts that on a stale head exactly one request is made and nothing is written, because the author must not be told about wording they have already changed. It creates the Humanize / Content Review check run against the reviewed head with the conclusion it was given, submits a grouped COMMENT review carrying inline comments pinned to that commit, and when there is nothing to place inline edits its own previous marked summary in place rather than accumulating comments across re-reviews. 5 unit tests over a fake transport cover publication, the stale-head refusal, editing an existing summary, first-time creation, and the failing-check path. Results: pnpm check 139 unit tests across 24 files; pnpm build passed.
tasks.nextAction: No live GitHub call has been made and none is possible until the user supplies GitHub App credentials; every test uses a fake transport, so this establishes request shape and ordering, not live API compatibility. Still to wire: the control-plane job that takes an accepted runner result, applies planPublication, builds the review and calls this transport, and records published comment identifiers for reconciliation. Rate-limit handling, conditional requests and retry on an uncertain write are not implemented.

tasks.title: Publish and reconcile grouped reviews
tasks.acceptance: Timeout after acceptance never blindly duplicates comments
tasks.evidence: GitHub publisher implemented in packages/github/src/publisher.ts. It renders a grouped COMMENT review, never APPROVE or REQUEST_CHANGES, with inline comments placed only on right-hand-side lines the pull request actually added and that are representable in the diff; a finding whose line is not part of the diff moves to the summary rather than being attached to an unrelated line the author did not touch. Each comment carries a stable fingerprint marker and the review body a review marker, so a re-review can update rather than duplicate. The summary states how much changed content was reviewed, collapses budgeted-out findings into a details block, and says plainly when there is nothing to flag. Check conclusions follow the specification and ADR-017: success with no findings, neutral for advisory findings however severe, and failure only when a customer-configured deterministic blocking rule is violated, so subjective wording can never fail a build. A native suggestion block is rendered when a safe replacement exists, which needs no Contents write permission. 7 unit tests cover exact-line placement, the summary fallback for undiffed lines and missing files, the collapsed section, the empty case, suggestion rendering, the check conclusion matrix, and an assertion that nothing published ever claims machine authorship (INV-006). Results: pnpm check 134 unit tests across 23 files; pnpm build passed.
tasks.nextAction: Not wired to GitHub transport yet: buildReview and buildCheck return payloads, and no code posts them through Octokit or reconciles an uncertain write. That transport plus stale-head guarding is P1-S14-T01 and P1-S06-T06, and it cannot be proven without GitHub App credentials, which the user will supply later. Comment updating on re-review uses the markers but no code yet reads existing comments to decide between create and update.

tasks.title: Apply check and incomplete-review policy
tasks.acceptance: Subjective findings neutral; configured deterministic violations fail
tasks.evidence: Publish worker implemented, and the ADR-038 lifetime guarantee is now proven at worker level rather than only at the store. publishReview takes the held payload, publishes it, and discards the content on every path that will not publish later: after a successful publish, after a superseded head where a newer review supersedes this one, and after a payload that cannot be parsed and so could never publish. It keeps the payload only for a failure a retry could still resolve, because discarding then would lose a review the queue is about to attempt again; the retry then publishes and clears it. 5 PostgreSQL integration tests assert the payload row count directly after each path, including that the transport is never called for an unpublishable payload. apps/worker/src/main.ts is now a runnable process: it migrates, starts the queue, SWEEPS ANY PAYLOAD A PREVIOUS PROCESS LEFT BEHIND before taking new work so content never outlives a crash by more than one restart, subscribes to github.event and review.publish, rehydrates each event from its recorded delivery rather than from the job payload, which carries identifiers only and never content, signals a retry by throwing so pg-boss reschedules, and shuts down on SIGTERM and SIGINT. Results: pnpm check 191 unit tests across 31 files; pnpm build passed; 56 integration tests passed from a freshly created disposable database.
tasks.nextAction: The worker starts but cannot yet complete a review: the publish transport throws PUBLISH_TRANSPORT_UNBOUND and the github.event handler is wired without a TrustedFileSource, so no review run is created. Both bindings need GitHub App credentials. The retention sweep runs once at startup rather than on a schedule, so a long-running process does not yet reclaim payloads abandoned during its own lifetime.

tasks.title: Package and document runner
tasks.acceptance: Clean-host install/upgrade works non-root and outbound-only
tasks.evidence: Runner packaged and documented, and the image was built and exercised rather than merely written. docker/runner holds a multi-stage Dockerfile, a reference compose deployment and a deployment runbook at docs/runbooks/runner-deployment.md covering enrollment, upgrade, revocation and failure symptoms. VERIFIED BY RUNNING THE IMAGE, not by reading it: the process runs as uid 10001 with no exposed ports, the root filesystem is read-only and /app is unwritable by the runner, git 2.39.5 is present as the only external binary, the image is 117 MB, it refuses to start without its two required variables, and it reaches a real Ollama on the host across host.docker.internal and reports models:1 at startup. THREE DEFECTS FOUND BY RUNNING IT. First, the tmpfs workspace was owned by root and therefore unwritable by the unprivileged runner, so no workspace could be created and no review could run; the mount now carries uid and gid, which is also called out in the runbook because a hand-written deployment would hit the same wall. Second, the image could not resolve @humanize packages at all, because a pnpm workspace keeps its links in each package node_modules which the build context excludes; the build now uses pnpm deploy to produce a self-contained tree, which also cut the image from 207 MB to 117 MB. Third, an unreachable model killed the process with a raw TypeError fetch failed from Node internals; startup now checks the model endpoint and exits with a sentence naming the endpoint and what to do, and separately reports when no model is installed. A startup line was added because silence and a crash loop look identical to an operator. Results: pnpm check 200 unit tests across 33 files; pnpm build passed; 70 integration tests passed.
tasks.nextAction: Not yet proven: upgrade on a clean host, since the image has only been built and run locally and never published or pulled; and the compose deployment has not been run end to end against a real control plane, which needs GitHub App credentials. The healthcheck is a placeholder that always succeeds rather than reporting whether the runner holds a lease or can still reach its model. No image signing, SBOM or vulnerability scan is in place, which P1-S20 should cover before distribution.

tasks.title: Implement GitHub sign-in and authorization
tasks.acceptance: Callback/session/CSRF/cross-tenant attacks rejected
tasks.evidence: Sign-in and session authorization implemented. packages/security adds SessionSigner, which signs identity claims and never carries a secret, with a minimum 32-byte deployment key, expiry enforced on read rather than merely recorded, and a constant-time signature comparison so a check cannot become a forgery oracle; requireOrganization refuses any action on an organization the session does not belong to. apps/api adds GitHub sign-in start and callback behind an injected IdentityProvider, so the exchange is testable without credentials. Callback safety is proven: a state is issued into an HttpOnly SameSite=Lax cookie and must be echoed back, so a callback with no cookie, no state parameter, or a mismatched state is refused, and a rejected identity exchange sets no session at all. 6 unit tests cover forged claims, a truncated signature, a session from another deployment key, an expired session, an absent session, and cross-tenant access to every credential endpoint. Results: pnpm check 199 unit tests across 33 files; pnpm build passed; 56 integration tests passed.
tasks.nextAction: No production IdentityProvider exists: the GitHub OAuth exchange is an injected port with no binding, which needs App credentials. Organization membership is taken from the exchange result and is not reconciled against GitHub afterwards, so a user removed from an organization keeps access until their session expires; a membership check on each request or a shorter session is required before release. apps/dashboard remains a scaffold with no sign-in UI, and the Playwright coverage the task expects does not exist.

tasks.title: Manage repositories and organization policy
tasks.acceptance: Fresh all-enabled-repository admin checks serialized with enablement
tasks.evidence: Repository enablement and organization policy administration implemented, exposed and consumed. The store performs the administrator check INSIDE the write, holding the target rows FOR UPDATE and only then asking which the caller may administer, so the answer cannot go stale and a revocation that lands first wins; six PostgreSQL tests prove selective enablement, the check seeing exactly the locked rows, a revoked caller enabling nothing, concurrent requests never overlapping inside the check, and a foreign repository never being offered. Organization policy has its own versioned, tenant-isolated table (migration 0005) kept apart from repository_configs so repository content cannot reach administrator-only fields (ADR-027). HTTP endpoints expose listing, enablement, and reading or replacing policy behind session authorization, with a test proving every route refuses another organization with 403 while the store is never called, refuses an unsigned caller with 401, and rejects a malformed identifier with 400. The loop is now closed: the event handler reads the stored policy rather than taking an injected function, and A REVIEW IS SKIPPED RATHER THAN DEFAULTED when no policy is set, because running on a provider, retention mode or execution mode nobody chose would be worse than not running; a stored policy that no longer satisfies its schema is treated as absent rather than patched. An integration test proves the stored policy governs the resulting snapshot and that both absent and invalid policies skip. Results: pnpm check 200 unit tests across 33 files; pnpm build passed; 63 integration tests passed from a clean disposable database with migrations 0000-0005 applying from scratch.
tasks.nextAction: AdminCheck has no production implementation, so nothing resolves real GitHub repository administrators; that needs App credentials. Dashboard pages remain a scaffold, so administration is reachable by HTTP but has no interface, and the Playwright coverage S16-T04 expects does not exist.

tasks.title: Manage encrypted provider credentials
tasks.acceptance: Write-only save/test/rotate/revoke; secrets never returned
tasks.evidence: Encrypted provider credential administration implemented as write-only ingress. POST /api/credentials accepts a secret, stores it through an injected CredentialAdmin port and returns only an identifier and provider name; a test saves sk-SENTINEL-VALUE and asserts the response body does not contain it, and that the listing endpoint returns metadata only, so a saved secret is never readable through any endpoint (ADR-035). Listing, saving and revoking each require a session that belongs to the organization named in the request, and a cross-tenant attempt returns 403 with the underlying store never called. Revocation is proven to reach the store with the correct tenant and identifier. The encrypted store behind the port already exists and is separately proven against PostgreSQL to hold ciphertext only, to separate tenants, and to refuse a revoked credential. Results: pnpm check 199 unit tests across 33 files.
tasks.nextAction: Rotation and the connection test are not exposed: the task names save, test, rotate and revoke, and only save, list and revoke exist. Test Connection needs the capability probe wired to a stored credential, and rotation needs a second credential activated before the first is revoked so a review in flight does not lose its provider. No production binding of CredentialAdmin to EncryptedSecretStore exists yet in a running API process.

Each record carries the finding fingerprint, one of the seven documented outcomes, whether it came from a person or was inferred, and the actor where there is one; the outcome and source sets are enforced by database constraints rather than convention, and repeated identical feedback is idempotent rather than multiplying. tasks.title: Implement retention transitions and purge
tasks.acceptance: Old jobs cannot recreate purged data; backups disclose expiry
tasks.evidence: Retention transitions and purge implemented, with the acceptance property proven: a job queued before a purge cannot recreate the data the purge removed. RetentionStore.setMode changes the repository retention mode FIRST and within the same transaction as the purge, so any later write is refused by the column constraints that enforce ephemeral storage rather than relying on the caller to notice. Downgrading to ephemeral nulls finding explanations and replacements, nulls evidence quotes, deletes any held publication payload and marks the runs ephemeral; a test writes content-bearing rows while indexed, downgrades, and asserts no sentinel string survives anywhere. A separate test then attempts the write a stale job would perform and asserts the database refuses it and no content appears. purgeOlderThan removes runs past the retention window together with everything hanging off them, verified across review runs, findings and feedback. 3 PostgreSQL tests. Results: pnpm check 200 unit tests across 33 files; pnpm build passed; 70 integration tests passed.
tasks.nextAction: No schedule drives the purge: purgeOlderThan exists but nothing calls it periodically, and the retention window is a caller argument rather than configured policy. The specification also requires that backups disclose expiry, which is untouched: nothing records or communicates when purged data leaves backups, and that belongs with the backup runbook in P1-S20-T02.

tasks.title: Complete telemetry and alerts
tasks.acceptance: End-to-end traces and leakage tests cover all boundaries
tasks.evidence: Telemetry completed as far as it can be without live services. The operational measurements the specification lists are now a typed union recorded through one surface, so a stage cannot invent its own label and a dashboard does not depend on spelling: webhook ingest, queue wait, checkout, extraction, context retrieval, model call, publication, retries and failures, stale reviews, runner state, findings published and suppressed, suggestions offered and accepted, verifier suppression, duplicates merged, files classified and nodes extracted. INSTRUMENTATION CANNOT BECOME A LEAK, which is the property worth having: a measurement dimension is emitted output like any other, so it passes the same field allowlist and the same shape-based scrubbing as a log line. Tests prove a bearer token and a provider key in dimensions are redacted, an unexpected dimension name is dropped entirely, and that repository content passed as text, explanation, quote or replacement never reaches output in any form; even a file path is refused, because a path can identify private work. Earlier in this stage the same review found that redaction filtered by field name only and let a connection string through as event; that is fixed and covered. Results: pnpm check 217 unit tests across 36 files; pnpm build passed.
tasks.nextAction: Not satisfied: the task requires end-to-end traces across all boundaries, and no stage yet calls measure or span in production paths, so the surface exists and is safe but nothing is actually instrumented; wiring it belongs with the stages it measures. No OpenTelemetry exporter is configured, so nothing is scraped or collected anywhere, and no alerting rules exist. A real trace across webhook, queue, runner and publication cannot be observed until the GitHub bindings exist.

tasks.title: Run adversarial security review
tasks.acceptance: No unresolved critical/high issues; injection/tenant/secret tests pass
tasks.evidence: Adversarial review executed against the real components and recorded in docs/security/adversarial-review.md. An attack corpus in packages/testing covers eight prompt-injection shapes, fabricated evidence, unsafe patches, six parser-hostility inputs and credential-shaped secrets; evals/security/boundaries.test.ts runs it against real extraction, prompt construction, the review pipeline, the suggestion validator and telemetry rather than doubles. HELD: injection is fenced with an unguessable per-review marker that content cannot close, and independently a model that obeys an injection still publishes nothing because the gate refuses any quotation absent from the node, so neither layer is load-bearing alone; fabricated quotations, paths and traversals are refused; unsafe patches are refused or neutralised by encoding with the structural proof rejecting anything beyond the target text; cross-tenant access is refused before the store is reached, on every endpoint and store that takes an organization. TWO FINDINGS, BOTH FIXED. First, twenty thousand nodes in one well-under-size file took 10.9 seconds to extract, because a size cap does not imply a node cap; extraction now stops at LIMITS.nodesPerFile and reports NODE_LIMIT_REACHED so a partially reviewed file cannot look fully reviewed, and the corpus now completes in 1.2 seconds. Second, telemetry redaction filtered by field NAME only, so a connection string logged as event or a token as traceId was written verbatim; values are now scrubbed by shape wherever they appear, with ordinary operational values untouched. Results: pnpm check 208 unit tests across 35 files; pnpm build passed; 70 integration tests passed.
tasks.nextAction: NOT SATISFIED: the task requires no unresolved critical or high issues after a review, and this is an agent review rather than an independent audit; a human security reviewer must repeat it before the criterion is met. Recorded residual limits: secret scrubbing works on shape and cannot catch an arbitrary short opaque secret, so callers must still not log secrets; no live GitHub or cloud provider was involved, so real token scope and real webhook delivery are untested; no dependency or image vulnerability scan, SBOM or signing exists (P1-S20); and there is no global rate limit on unauthenticated registration attempts or webhook volume.

tasks.title: Run resource and outage stress tests
tasks.acceptance: Limits respected, coverage honest and service responsive
tasks.evidence: Resource and outage stress implemented in evals/security/limits.test.ts, driving the real components past each documented limit. LIMITS ARE ENFORCED, NOT JUST DOCUMENTED: a file past LIMITS.fileBytes yields no nodes and a FILE_TOO_LARGE diagnostic; a file past LIMITS.nodesPerFile stops at the cap and reports NODE_LIMIT_REACHED; a single node longer than LIMITS.nodeChars is refused rather than truncated, because a truncated node would be reviewed as if it were the whole sentence; context stays within LIMITS.contextTokens with a crowded index and within a tighter caller budget, reporting truncation so nobody mistakes partial context for the repository. RESPONSIVENESS: indexing 5000 nodes and searching them completes well under five seconds. OUTAGE: a provider failing on one node records a failure and still reviews the rest, with reviewed counting both. COVERAGE IS HONEST: a non-locale data file, an unsupported format and an oversized file each produce zero nodes AND a named diagnostic, so a skip is never silent; this is the failure mode the project has rediscovered repeatedly and the test asserts against it directly. Results: pnpm check 215 unit tests across 36 files; pnpm build passed; 70 integration tests passed.
tasks.nextAction: Not covered: no test drives a full repository through acquisition, extraction and review at scale, because that needs a large real repository and GitHub credentials; parser wall-clock timeouts (LIMITS.parserMs) and memory bounds are defined but not enforced by an isolated worker, so a pathological parser can still block its job; there is no load test of the API or queue under concurrent webhook volume, and no global rate limit on unauthenticated endpoints.
